ports.name: DMA1 address/count
ports.detail: Channels 0-3 (8-bit DMA): even port = base/current address, odd port = base/current count. Each is 16 bits written low byte then high byte through the byte-pointer flip-flop.
notes: Write 0x0C first to reset the flip-flop so the low byte goes first.

ports.name: DMA1 status
ports.detail: Bits 3:0 terminal count reached on channels 3-0, bits 7:4 request pending.

ports.name: DMA1 command
ports.detail: Controller command register; the PC BIOS leaves it at 0.

ports.name: DMA1 request
ports.detail: Software DMA request: bits 1:0 channel, bit 2 set/clear.

ports.name: DMA1 clear byte pointer flip-flop
ports.detail: Any value written resets the flip-flop so the next address/count byte is the low byte.

ports.name: DMA1 intermediate
ports.detail: Temporary register (memory-to-memory transfers, unused on PCs).

ports.name: DMA1 master clear
ports.detail: Any value written resets the controller and masks all four channels.

ports.name: DMA1 clear mask
ports.detail: Any value written unmasks all four channels.

ports.name: DMA1 write all masks
ports.detail: Bits 3:0 mask channels 3-0.

ports.name: PIC1 status
ports.detail: Reads IRR or ISR, whichever the last OCW3 selected (IRR after reset).

ports.name: PIC1 command
ports.detail: Bit 4 set = ICW1 (start initialisation); otherwise bit 3 selects OCW3 (1) or OCW2 (0).
notes: Send EOI (0x20) to both PICs for IRQ 8-15: slave first, then master.

ports.name: PIC1 data
ports.detail: Outside initialisation: the interrupt mask register, bit n masks IRQ n. During initialisation: ICW2 (vector base, multiple of 8), ICW3 (bit 2 = slave on IR2), ICW4 (bit 0 = 8086 mode).
notes: The BIOS programs vector base 0x08, which collides with CPU exceptions in protected mode; remap before enabling interrupts.

ports.name: PIC2 status
ports.detail: Reads IRR or ISR, whichever the last OCW3 selected.

ports.name: PIC2 command
ports.detail: As port 0x20, for IRQ 8-15.

ports.name: PIC2 data
ports.detail: Bit n masks IRQ 8+n. ICW2 vector base (BIOS: 0x70), ICW3 = cascade identity 2, ICW4 bit 0 = 8086 mode.

ports.name: ELCR1
ports.detail: Bit n set = IRQ n level-triggered. IRQ 0, 1, 2, 8 and 13 must stay edge.
ports.confidence: chipset register, present on PCI-era PCs, absent on ISA-only machines

ports.name: ELCR2
ports.detail: Bit n set = IRQ 8+n level-triggered.
ports.confidence: chipset register, present on PCI-era PCs, absent on ISA-only machines

ports.name: PIT counter 0
ports.detail: System timer, wired to IRQ0. The BIOS runs it in mode 3 with divisor 0 (65536): 18.2065 Hz. Input clock 1.193182 MHz.
notes: Write the count in the order the control word's access mode selects (lobyte then hibyte for mode 3).

ports.name: PIT counter 1
ports.detail: DRAM refresh on the PC/AT; not usable on later machines.

ports.name: PIT counter 2
ports.detail: PC speaker tone and a polled timer; gated by port 0x61 bit 0, output readable at 0x61 bit 5.

ports.name: KBC data
ports.detail: Read: the output buffer (scan code, or a controller command's reply) once status bit 0 is set. Write: a byte for the keyboard, or the parameter of the last controller command (0x60, 0xD1 ...), once status bit 1 is clear.
notes: After command 0xD1 the next byte written here becomes the output port: 0xDF enables A20, 0xDD disables it (bit 0 must stay 1 or the CPU resets).

ports.name: KBC status

fields.name: OBF
fields.desc: output buffer full: data waiting at 0x60

fields.name: IBF
fields.desc: input buffer full: do not write 0x60/0x64 yet

fields.name: SYS
fields.desc: system flag, set after a successful self test

fields.name: CMD
fields.desc: last write went to 0x64 (command) rather than 0x60

notes: Poll IBF (bit 1) clear before every write to 0x60 or 0x64, with a timeout: some machines have no 8042 and read 0xFF forever.

ports.name: KBC command

values.name: write controller command byte (next byte to 0x60)
write next byte to aux device

notes: 0xDD/0xDF are not standard 8042 commands; use 0xD1 + output port 0xDF to be portable.
0xFE resets the CPU; it is the classic reboot path when 0xCF9 is absent.

ports.name: System control port B

fields.name: REFRESH
fields.desc: read: toggles every refresh cycle (about 15 us), used as a delay source

notes: Read-modify-write: only bits 3:0 are writable, and the upper bits read back status.

ports.name: CMOS index
ports.long: RTC/CMOS register select and NMI mask

fields.name: INDEX
fields.desc: CMOS register for the next 0x71 access

values.name: status B (SET 7, PIE 6, AIE 5, UIE 4, SQWE 3, DM binary 2, 24h 1, DSE 0)
status C (IRQF 7, PF 6, AF 5, UF 4; read clears)
shutdown status (0x00 normal POST, 0x05 jump via 40:67 with EOI, 0x09 block move return, 0x0A jump via 40:67 without EOI)
extended memory found by POST, low
extended memory found by POST, high
century (IBM AT; ACPI FADT names the real one)

notes: Write 0x70 then access 0x71 immediately; an interrupt in between can retarget the index.
Bit 7 masks NMI for as long as it stays set: write the index with bit 7 clear afterwards, or NMI stays off.
Time registers are BCD unless status B bit 2 is set; read only when status A bit 7 (UIP) is clear.

ports.name: CMOS data
ports.detail: Reads or writes the register selected through port 0x70.

ports.name: CMOS index (bank 1)
ports.detail: Index for the upper 128 bytes of CMOS RAM on chipsets that have them.

ports.name: CMOS data (bank 1)
ports.detail: Data for the upper 128 bytes of CMOS RAM.

ports.name: POST code
ports.detail: Write-only: the byte appears on a POST card's display. Writing it takes about 1 us on ISA timing, so `outb %al, $0x80` is the traditional I/O delay.
notes: Some hypervisors and boards forward 0x80 elsewhere; use it only as a delay or diagnostic.

ports.name: DMA page channel 2
ports.detail: Address bits 23:16 for DMA channel 2 (floppy).

ports.name: DMA page channel 3
ports.detail: Address bits 23:16 for DMA channel 3.

ports.name: DMA page channel 1
ports.detail: Address bits 23:16 for DMA channel 1.

ports.name: DMA page channel 0
ports.detail: Address bits 23:16 for DMA channel 0.

ports.name: DMA page channel 6
ports.detail: Address bits 23:17 for 16-bit DMA channel 6.

ports.name: DMA page channel 7
ports.detail: Address bits 23:17 for 16-bit DMA channel 7.

ports.name: DMA page channel 5
ports.detail: Address bits 23:17 for 16-bit DMA channel 5.

ports.name: DMA page channel 4
ports.detail: Refresh / cascade page register; unused on PCs.

ports.name: System control port A
notes: Read-modify-write and clear bit 0 before writing back: `orb $0x02, %al; andb $0xFE, %al`. Setting it reboots the machine.
Not present on every machine; some read back 0xFF. Verify A20 by a wrap test.

ports.name: DMA2 address/count
ports.detail: Channels 4-7 (16-bit DMA). Registers sit on even ports: 0xC0/0xC2 channel 4 address/count, 0xC4/0xC6 channel 5, 0xC8/0xCA channel 6, 0xCC/0xCE channel 7. Addresses and counts are in words.

ports.name: DMA2 status/command
ports.detail: As port 0x08 for channels 4-7.

ports.name: DMA2 single channel mask
ports.detail: As port 0x0A; channel 4 is the cascade from controller 1 and must stay unmasked.

ports.name: DMA2 mode
ports.detail: As port 0x0B.

ports.name: QEMU isa-debug-exit
ports.detail: With `-device isa-debug-exit` (default iobase 0xF4): writing v exits QEMU with status (v << 1) | 1.
ports.confidence: emulator only, and only when the device is configured

ports.name: VGA CRTC index (mono)
ports.detail: CRTC index when misc output bit 0 = 0 (monochrome addressing); same registers as 0x3D4.

ports.name: VGA input status 1 (mono)
ports.detail: As 0x3DA under monochrome addressing; reading it resets the attribute flip-flop.

ports.name: VGA attribute index/data
ports.detail: Alternates between index and data on each write, tracked by a flip-flop that a read of 0x3DA (0x3BA mono) resets to index. Index bit 5 (PAS) must be set again afterwards or the screen stays blank.

fields.name: RAM_EN
fields.desc: enable CPU access to video RAM

ports.name: VGA sequencer data
ports.detail: The register selected through 0x3C4.

ports.name: VGA DAC pixel mask
ports.detail: ANDed with each pixel value before palette lookup; leave at 0xFF.

ports.name: VGA DAC state
ports.detail: Bits 1:0: 0 = DAC in write mode, 3 = read mode.

ports.name: VGA DAC read index
ports.detail: Palette entry for the next three 0x3C9 reads (R, G, B).

ports.name: VGA DAC write index
ports.detail: Palette entry for the next three 0x3C9 writes (R, G, B, 6 bits each); auto-increments.

ports.name: VGA DAC data
ports.detail: Red, green, blue in turn, 6 bits each in standard VGA.

ports.name: VGA misc output read
ports.detail: Reads back the value written to 0x3C2.

ports.name: VGA CRTC index
ports.detail: A 16-bit write puts the index in the low byte and the data in the high byte (0x3D5) in one access.

ports.name: VGA CRTC data
ports.detail: The register selected through 0x3D4.

ports.name: VGA input status 1
notes: Reading it resets the attribute controller flip-flop at 0x3C0 to index.

fields.name: DIO
fields.desc: 1 = controller has data for the CPU

ports.name: FDC data FIFO
ports.detail: Command bytes, parameters and results; check RQM (and DIO) in 0x3F4 before each byte.

ports.name: FDC digital input
notes: Shares its address with the primary IDE channel's obsolete drive address register.

ports.name: QEMU/OVMF debug console
ports.detail: Bytes written appear on the debug console when QEMU runs with `-device isa-debugcon,iobase=0x402` (OVMF's debug port). Reads return 0xE9 when the device is present.
ports.confidence: emulator only, and only when configured

ports.name: QEMU fw_cfg selector
ports.detail: 16-bit selector for the fw_cfg item read through 0x511.

ports.name: QEMU fw_cfg data
ports.detail: Byte stream of the selected fw_cfg item.

ports.name: Bochs/QEMU debug port
ports.device: Bochs port E9 hack / QEMU isa-debugcon
ports.detail: Bytes written appear on the emulator's debug console (Bochs `port_e9_hack`, QEMU `-debugcon`). Reads return 0xE9 when present.

ports.name: PCI CONFIG_ADDRESS

fields.name: EXT_REG
fields.desc: extended register bits 11:8 (AMD and some Intel chipsets only)
fields.confidence: chipset-specific, reserved in the PCI spec

fields.name: ENABLE
fields.desc: 1 = the next 0xCFC access is a configuration cycle

notes: Only a 32-bit access to 0xCF8 is a CONFIG_ADDRESS write; byte or word writes pass through as ordinary I/O (a byte write to 0xCF9 is the reset control register).
Interrupts and other CPUs can change CONFIG_ADDRESS between the 0xCF8 write and the 0xCFC access; hold a lock or keep interrupts off.

ports.name: Reset control

fields.name: SYS_RST
fields.desc: 1 = hard (system) reset, 0 = soft reset (INIT) when RST_CPU fires

fields.name: RST_CPU
fields.desc: 0 -> 1 transition triggers the reset SYS_RST selects

notes: Write 0x02 then 0x06: the reset fires on the 0 -> 1 transition of bit 2.
Byte access only; a dword access at 0xCF8 is CONFIG_ADDRESS.
ports.confidence: chipset register: present on PCI-era chipsets from PIIX on, not architectural

ports.name: PCI CONFIG_DATA
ports.detail: The configuration register CONFIG_ADDRESS selected. Byte and word accesses use 0xCFC + (offset & 3): a word at offset 0x02 is `inw $0xCFE`.
notes: Reads of a missing device return all ones (vendor ID 0xFFFF).

blocks.name: 16550 UART
notes: Bases are the BIOS defaults; the BIOS data area at 40:00 lists the ports it actually found.
COM1/COM3 share IRQ4 and COM2/COM4 share IRQ3. Divisor = 115200 / baud.

regs.name: RBR
regs.detail: Received byte; valid when LSR bit 0 (DR) is set.

regs.name: THR
regs.detail: Byte to send; write only when LSR bit 5 (THRE) is set.

regs.name: DLL
regs.detail: Low byte of the baud divisor (115200 / baud).

regs.name: DLM
regs.detail: High byte of the baud divisor.

fields.name: OUT2
fields.desc: gates the IRQ line on PCs

regs.name: LSR

fields.name: THRE
fields.desc: THR empty: may write the next byte

notes: Reads 0xFF when no UART is present: test for that before polling THRE, or the loop exits immediately.

blocks.name: Parallel port
notes: LPT numbering follows the BIOS data area at 40:08, not the base: with an MDA card present 0x3BC is LPT1.

regs.name: DATA
regs.detail: Output latch; readable back, and an input when control bit 5 is set on a bidirectional port.

fields.name: BIDIR
fields.desc: data port is an input (PS/2 bidirectional)

blocks.name: ATA command block
notes: IDE0 = primary channel (IRQ14, control at 0x3F6), IDE1 = secondary (IRQ15, control at 0x376). PCI IDE controllers in native mode use BAR-assigned ports instead.
Select the drive (+6), wait 400 ns (read the alternate status four times), then wait for BSY clear before issuing a command.

regs.name: DATA
regs.detail: PIO data, 16 bits per transfer (`rep insw`). 32-bit access only where the controller supports it.

fields.name: TK0NF
fields.desc: track 0 not found / end of media

regs.name: FEATURES
regs.detail: Command-specific parameter (SET FEATURES subcommand, PACKET DMA flag).

regs.name: SECTOR COUNT
regs.detail: 0 means 256 sectors (65536 with the 48-bit commands). 48-bit commands take two writes: high byte, then low.

regs.name: LBA MID
regs.detail: ATAPI devices leave 0x14 here (and 0xEB at LBA HIGH) after reset or a failed IDENTIFY.

regs.name: STATUS

fields.name: DRQ
fields.desc: data request: ready for PIO transfer

fields.name: BSY
fields.desc: busy: every other bit is invalid while set

notes: Reading STATUS acknowledges the device interrupt; read the alternate status (0x3F6/0x376) to poll without doing so.
0xFF means a floating bus (no device); 0x00 after a select usually means no device too.

regs.name: ALT STATUS
regs.detail: Same bits as STATUS, without acknowledging the interrupt: use it for the 400 ns delay and for polling.

fields.name: SRST
fields.desc: software reset of both devices on the channel (hold 5 us)

fields.name: HOB
fields.desc: read back the high-order bytes of a 48-bit command
